newsitem.title: USA: 'I thought I was going to die,' Fran survivor says.
newsitem.headline: 'I thought I was going to die,' Fran survivor says.

text.p: At the height of Hurricane Fran's fury, Daniel Gulker called 911 to ask authorities to contact his relatives in case of his death.
"I want to give a message for my next of kin," Gulker, 34, told the dispatcher. "I don't think we're going to make it."

When Hurricane Fran swept ashore late on Thursday, it hit Carolina Beach, on Pleasure Island off Wilmington, with 100 mph (160 kph) winds and a tidal surge that sent a wall of water right across the narrow strip of land.
The rising water forced Gulker and his girlfriend, Valerie Patterson, 34, out of her first-floor beachfront condominium into his, on the second floor.
"It's up to our porch now. Everything's going. The building's starting to fall apart," Gulker told the dispatcher.
Two days later, he called his decision to remain on the island while others followed mandatory evacuation orders "the stupidest thing I've ever done."
Gulker said the storm surge was so strong it lifted cars and dumpsters and slammed them into the building, shaking the walls and convincing him that the structure was collapsing.
"I thought I was going to die. There were trucks and cars floating by us. The water was coming over the building. It must have been 18 feet high," he said. "I've never been so scared in my life."
He had made the decision to ride out the storm at home in part to remain with his golden retriever, named "Sandy Beach Carolina." Animals are not welcomed at public shelters during hurricanes.
"We love her," he said, adding that next time, he will follow evacuation orders and leave the island. "Nobody should ever be as stupid as we were."
